dedupe_keys.name: 25 verde tree house residential building in torino heat adaptation with greenery and thermal mass climate adapt

description: This Climate-ADAPT case study presents 25 Verde, a residential building in Torino, Italy, designed by the Luciano Pia architecture studio to cope with rising summer temperatures while cutting energy use. Design ran from 2007 to 2010 and construction from 2010 to 2012. Measures combine high thermal mass (35 cm solid floor slabs and thick brick walls), continuous external insulation and a ventilated facade, louvres and deciduous plants for summer shading, large glazing for winter gains, a green roof with a thick soil layer, and high-efficiency heat pumps using groundwater for heating and cooling, so the building has no direct CO2 emissions. It cost about EUR 2,500 per square metre, double a standard building, with greenery 10-15% of the total; it was rated energy class A, received a 20% construction tax discount, and flats sold at about EUR 5,500 per square metre. Coverage: one building, set against regional projections of summer maximum temperatures rising from 28 °C to 30-32 °C. Access: the case study page, published on 18 October 2019 and modified on 25 August 2026. Licence: Climate-ADAPT content under the EEA reuse policy; free. Caveats: benefits are described qualitatively from resident feedback; no monitored indoor temperature series is given. Simulation uses are a design reference for modelling green envelopes and thermal mass against heatwaves. Related records: the Madrid IMDEA Energy building and Reggio Emilia roof retrofit case studies.
name: 25 Verde 'tree house' residential building in Torino: heat adaptation with greenery and thermal mass (Climate-ADAPT)
outcomes: A residential building completed in 2012 with 35 cm slabs, ventilated facades, deciduous planting, a green roof and groundwater heat pumps; it cost about EUR 2,500 per square metre, double a standard building, with greenery 10-15% of the cost, reached energy class A and is expected to last about 50 years.
